newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Nanjing Panda sees improving conditions.
newsitem.headline: Nanjing Panda sees improving conditions.

text.p: Chinese television maker Nanjing Panda Electronics Co Ltd said on Wednesday it expected its operating environment to improve in the second half.
"We're confident of achieving our (profit) target for 1996," president Lu Rongchang told a news conference.

The company, listed in Hong Kong in May, posted net profit of 86.45 million yuan in the first half of this year. Pre-tax profit rose 10.7 percent to 101 million yuan. Lu said the firm had achieved 40 percent of its targeted 1996 profit.

He expected the operating environment to improve in the second half. Gross margin would improve because material costs, which had been falling in the first half, were expected to stay at low levels and selling prices were expected to be stable.

The company's gross margin fell about 2.4 percentage points year-on-year in the first half. It had held at about 15 percent in past years. Lu said the firm had made some price adjustments in the first half amid a television price war in China.
Its market share in China stood at 11.6 percent in the period, versus about eight percent in full-year 1995, he said.
The company did not expect television prices to fluctuate greatly in the second half, Lu said, but it might cut the prices of some models.
